items.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I also had found Dave Frishberg so I learned “I’m Hip.”

ctx.x: Well I played in I think it was the beginning of college. Since I was already singing and playing in rock bands through high school, when I went to college I had my guitar and I had with me the Kenny Rankin album, I had some Michael Franks records, and some James Taylor stuff. And I had seen guys who sat and played the guitar, you know, folk guys. And so I learned some of these Kenny Rankin songs, like “Haven’t We Met” and he did “Here’s that Rainy Day,” and he did “Sunny Gets Blue” on this one record. And then I…

minutes and he’d say “sing, sing something.” And he’d say — and I’d do “Straighten Up and Fly Right,” “For Sentimental Reasons.” And then we would close out. We would do an Ellington medley and “Sing Sing Sing” or a little Goodman medley. And so as luck would have it, it’s amazing, it’s weird thinking about it because it’s so long ago to me now. In 1983, in May of ’83 I was singing this tune “I Like Jersey Best.” A buddy of mine wrote this song about our state, make a little rock & roll record with my friend…

items.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I have these quotes that I like to — I call it Random Quotes. One in particular, just so you know what I keep in here, it’s something Dave Frishberg said.

ctx.x: This — I have these quotes that I like to — I call it Random Quotes. One in particular, just so you know what I keep in here, it’s something Dave Frishberg said. He said, “Jazz musicians were hip. They were funny, they were sensitive, they were clannish, and they seemed to have the best girlfriends.” That’s something Dave Frishberg — just so you know what I have in here. But I have this quote from Joshua Redman. And I read it to Isaiah one night and he was like, “Can you send that to me?” And so he said, “I still…

aren’t playing music that is technically swing music, the ones that are good have dealt with that and have that as a basis in what they do. And if they want up on the bandstand on a jam session and the band was playing ‘C Jam Blues’ they could get up there and take a smoking solo on that.” And I think that’s the best explanation. You know so you have the knowledge of it at least. It’s not an excuse to say, “Oh I’m not going to do that.” I hope that made some sense.
